I didn't find a GitHub issue in these results that specifically covers React 19 hydration mismatches caused by browser extensions. Most hits are third-party mirrors or aggregators, so the official issue pages should be checked directly.

- **Older related issue:** A mirror of a React 16-era feature request says the checksum attribute was removed, so apps lost a way to detect mismatches. The solution does not necessarily need to re-introduce the checksum attribute again. It could be some other event, hook, or callback that applications can leverage to handle checksum issues.
- **Extension-related PR:** PR #24523 is the closest match. It concerns an extension breaking a React app during hydration. Its author notes that the change does not introduce compatibility with extensions or 3rd party scripts that modify the DOM before React hydrates, it simply inverts what gets broken.
- **Unrelated React 19 mismatch bug:** Issue #31317 is a regression in React 19.0.0 that logs spurious hydration warnings around Suspense boundaries, and it was fixed in 19.0.1. It doesn't involve extensions.
- **Error reporting change:** Commit #28502 changed how React reports mismatch diffs, so they are collected and passed to `onRecoverableError` rather than logged for every mismatch.
- **Unverified secondary claims:** Some skill-listing sites say React 19 is more tolerant of extra attributes added by extensions and recovers more granularly. These are not primary sources, so I'd treat them as unconfirmed.

Next step: search the facebook/react issue tracker directly for "extension" with "hydration" and the 19.x version tag.

The search turned up several reports of browser extensions causing hydration errors in React 19 apps, mostly through Next.js.

- **ColorZilla in Next.js 15 / React 19 RC:** The most detailed case is a Next.js discussion. The ColorZilla extension added a `cz-shortcut-listen` attribute, which caused a server/client mismatch, and the error went away when the extension was disabled. [GitHub, vercel/next.js #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035)
- **Official React issue:** facebook/react #25924 reports hydration errors from a script that the React DevTools extension injected after the body tag. That report was against React 18.2, not 19. [GitHub, facebook/react #25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924)
- **Grammarly and password managers:** Several blog posts say Grammarly adds `data-gramm` attributes to inputs before React hydrates, and that other extensions add attributes or elements the server HTML never had. These are secondary sources, so I'd treat them as explanations to verify rather than authoritative documentation. [Loke.dev](https://loke.dev/blog/fix-react-19-hydration-errors-boundary-issues), [NovaSphere](https://novasphereailab.com/blog/fix-react-hydration-errors)
- **React 19 changes:** One guide says React 19 skips unexpected tags appended to `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>`, but not attributes added to elements React already manages. That narrows the improvement considerably, and the guide notes reports continued through at least November 2025. [Nerdlevel Tech](https://nerdleveltech.com/react-hydration-mismatch)
- **Common workaround:** Several guides suggest `suppressHydrationWarning` on the affected element, and warn against using it to hide real bugs. [Skilldham](https://skilldham.com/blog/react-hydration-error-nextjs)

The search did not surface an official React document that specifically covers Grammarly or Dark Reader. The Grammarly attribute claims come from blog posts, not from Grammarly or React documentation.

content.text:
Yes, there are related issues. I didn't find one in the React repo that is specifically about React 19 and extensions.

- **Closest official issue:** [facebook/react #25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924), "Scripts injected by browser extensions (e.g. React dev tools) may cause hydration errors". It was reported against React 18.2, not 19. The cause is the same, an extension changing the DOM before hydration.
- **React 19 report, in Next.js:** [vercel/next.js Discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035). On Next.js 15 with React 19, the ColorZilla extension injects a `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute, which causes a hydration error. The error goes away when the extension is disabled.
- **Tooling fallout:** [getsentry/sentry-javascript #15886](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/issues/15886), "React 19 hydration error ignoring". I only saw the title, so I haven't confirmed it involves extensions.
- **Unchecked candidate:** [facebook/react #35219](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/35219) came up in the search, but GitHub returned a 403 when I fetched it. I don't know what it says.

I couldn't run a direct search of the facebook/react tracker, because the GitHub API returned 403 and `gh` isn't authenticated. A search on GitHub for `hydration extension` in facebook/react, filtered to 19.x, would be the way to check for a closer match.

The usual workaround is `suppressHydrationWarning` on the affected element, e.g. `<html>` or `<body>`. This only silences that element's own attribute and text mismatches, not mismatches inside its children.
